messages.text: Landed! Auntie, how is your world fund doing?
Strange. The fund says flat, but in yen I'm up a lot
That's the yen, not the fund
So I made money without the shares going up?

steps.prompt: In 2021 Michiko bought $10,000 of a fund at ¥110 per dollar. The fund is flat in dollars. Now a dollar costs ¥150. How much is it worth in yen, compared with what she paid?
steps.reveal: +36%. She paid ¥1.1 million, and the same $10,000 is now ¥1.5 million. The shares didn't move; the yen got weaker. Simplified from real data.

steps.title: The same door swings both ways
steps.body: Owning things priced in another currency adds [[currency-risk]]. A weaker yen made Michiko's foreign shares worth more in yen. If the yen gets stronger again, the same shares are worth fewer yen, even if they don't move at all.

steps.prompt: Match each idea from the Tokyo story with its meaning.
pairs: Exchange rates change the value in your money
A fall from a previous high

steps.prompt: The yen gets 20% stronger against the dollar. Michiko's dollar fund doesn't move. What happens in yen?
options: Her fund is worth fewer yen
Her fund is worth more yen
steps.explanation: Each dollar now buys fewer yen. A flat fund in dollars becomes a loss in yen. Currency moves can help or hurt; they rarely stay still.

messages.text: I'm here! Auntie, how is your world fund?
Strange. The fund didn't change, but in yen I have more
That's because of the yen, not the fund
So I won money but the shares didn't go up?

p1.prompt: In 2021 Michiko bought $10,000 of a fund. One dollar cost ¥110. The fund is still $10,000. Now one dollar costs ¥150. How much more or less is it in yen? Guess.
p1.reveal: +36%. She paid ¥1.1 million. Now the same $10,000 is ¥1.5 million. The shares stayed the same. The yen became weaker.

t1.title: It can go both ways
t1.body: If you own things in another currency, the exchange rate changes their value in your money. This is [[currency-risk]]. A weak yen helped Michiko. A strong yen would hurt her, even if the shares stay the same.

m1.prompt: Match each word with what it means.

q1.prompt: The yen gets 20% stronger. Michiko's dollar fund stays the same. What happens in yen?
options: Her fund is worth fewer yen
Her fund is worth more yen
q1.explanation: One dollar now gives fewer yen. So the same fund is worth less in yen.
